title: U.S. House · New York's 8th Congressional District
area: Central and southern Brooklyn, including Brownsville, East New York, Canarsie, Coney Island, and parts of Crown Heights.

context.text: Incumbent Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic Leader, advanced unopposed after the Democratic primary was canceled (challengers Vance Bostic and Chi Osse withdrew or were disqualified). Lewis Mizrahi advanced unopposed after the Republican and Conservative Party primaries were canceled.
Mizrahi also filed to run in New York's 9th Congressional District but was disqualified from that district's Republican primary; he remains on the ballot only in the 8th District.

candidates.name: Hakeem Jeffries

summary.text: Hakeem Jeffries is the incumbent U.S. Representative for NY-8 and the House Democratic Leader. A Brooklyn native and attorney, he served in the New York State Assembly from 2007 before his election to Congress in 2012, and has led House Democrats since being elected Democratic Leader in November 2022. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born August 4, 1970, in Brooklyn and raised in the Crown Heights neighborhood; graduated from Midwood High School in 1988.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from SUNY Binghamton (1992), a Master of Public Policy from Georgetown University (1994), and a J.D. from New York University School of Law (1997).

Clerked for U.S. District Judge Harold Baer Jr. in the Southern District of New York, then practiced at the law firm Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison (1998-2004); he also worked at Godosky & Gentile and later served as in-house litigation counsel for Viacom and CBS.

Represented the 57th District in the New York State Assembly beginning in 2007; his Assembly committee assignments included Judiciary, Codes, Correction, Housing and Banks. A 2010 law he sponsored with then-Sen. Eric Adams barred police from compiling the names and addresses of people stopped but not arrested.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2012 and took office in 2013. Early House committee assignments were Judiciary (including its courts, intellectual property and antitrust subcommittees) and Budget.

Elected chair of the House Democratic Caucus in November 2018 (123-113 over Rep. Barbara Lee) for the 116th Congress; his official biography also lists him as a former Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus and former co-chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee.
In January 2020, Speaker Nancy Pelosi named him one of seven House managers for the Senate impeachment trial of President Donald Trump.

His official biography describes him as lead Democratic sponsor of the FIRST STEP Act (signed December 2018), a participant in House passage of the Music Modernization Act (2018), and sponsor of the Keep America's Refuges Operational Act (2018).

Elected House Democratic Leader on November 30, 2022, running unopposed, and re-elected to the post on November 19, 2024; as Democratic Leader he serves on no standing committees. He was Democratic Leader during the 2025 federal government shutdown, which ran from October 1 to November 12, 2025.

priorities.text: His office lists affordable housing development, criminal justice system reform, prescription drug price reduction, and educational access and quality among his primary focus areas.
Describes his work as "fighting for everyday Americans" on health care costs, housing affordability, job creation, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.

record.text: Serves on no standing committees as House Democratic Leader for the 2023-2026 period, a customary practice for the top party leader in the chamber.

Introduced H.Res. 625, recognizing the 50th anniversary of the independence of the Republic of Cabo Verde, in the 119th Congress; most of his recently introduced measures in this Congress have been ceremonial resolutions rather than substantive legislation, consistent with his role setting the chamber's floor agenda as party leader rather than sponsoring bills.

candidates.researchNotes: As House Democratic Leader, Jeffries holds no committee assignments and has sponsored little substantive legislation in the current Congress (leadership duties like floor scheduling and caucus messaging are not individually documented with citable official records); floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Lewis Mizrahi

summary.text: Lewis Mizrahi is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee against incumbent Hakeem Jeffries in NY-8. Ballotpedia reports that he advanced from both party primaries without a contest, that he also sought the Republican nomination in NY-9 but was disqualified there, and that he has not completed its Candidate Connection survey. Little public biographical or campaign material about him could be found.

background.text: Advanced as the Republican and Conservative Party candidate for NY-8 after both June 23, 2026 primaries were canceled; he also filed to run in NY-9's Republican primary and was disqualified there.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey could be found for Lewis Mizrahi, and FEC data reported via Ballotpedia shows no campaign contributions as of the research date; the FEC's own candidate-search API could not be queried directly (requires an API key). He also filed to run in NY-9 but was disqualified from that district's Republican primary. A voter-guide aggregator (Smarter.Vote) attributed a Second Amendment position to Mizrahi citing a 2024 Adirondack Daily Enterprise article on far-right militia activity; that article, read directly, is about a different person (Nathan Mizrahi, of the Liberty State Militia) and does not concern this candidate, so it is not used here. No biographical details beyond ballot status could be confirmed from a primary or news source, so his biography is intentionally brief.
